Lewis Hamilton Secures Mexico City Pole as Antonelli Approaches Title Milestone

01 Nov 2026, 11:58 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.abc.net.au

2 min read

Key takeaways

Image: www.abc.net.au · Source image rights not independently verified · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9 for the website

  1. Qualifying Results and Historical Context
  2. Title Decider: Kimi Antonelli
  3. Performance Notes

Qualifying Results and Historical Context

Lewis Hamilton secured pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix, marking his 105th career pole and his first since joining Ferrari. At 41 years old, Hamilton becomes the oldest driver to claim pole position since Mario Andretti in 1982. This achievement follows a 1,197-day wait for a non-sprint race pole, with his previous top qualifying performance dating back to Hungary in July 2023.

Title Decider: Kimi Antonelli

All eyes are on 20-year-old Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who is positioned to potentially become the youngest Formula One world champion in history. Entering the weekend with a significant lead, Antonelli needs to finish ninth or higher to secure the championship.

  • Current Standing: Antonelli qualified fifth but will start fourth due to a grid penalty assessed to Max Verstappen.
  • Championship Stakes: If Antonelli finishes ninth or better, he will claim the title. He can also clinch the championship if neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton wins the race.
  • Historical Significance: Success for Antonelli would make him the first Italian champion since 1953.

Performance Notes

  • George Russell: The Mercedes driver secured the second-fastest time, remaining in contention to delay Antonelli's championship celebration.
  • Oscar Piastri: The Australian driver experienced a difficult qualifying session, finishing 13th and failing to advance to the final round. He cited a lack of rear grip as a primary issue during the session.
  • Field Notes: Charles Leclerc qualified third for Ferrari. Lando Norris, last year's winner, qualified sixth, while Ryo Hirakawa made his Formula One debut in 19th position for Haas.
  • Incidents: Fernando Alonso triggered a session suspension in the first phase due to a suspected water pressure issue and was subsequently noted for failing to reattach his steering wheel after exiting his vehicle.

Verification

Official timing sheets and full starting grids for the Mexico City Grand Prix are available via the official Formula 1 website and FIA communications. Fans can verify live race updates and specific grid adjustments by consulting official broadcast partners or the sport's governing body portals.
